full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha, J : This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.10.93 of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court Sylhet in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1988 (Family) reversing with modification those dated 30.6.88 of the learned Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court, Golapganj, Sylhet in Family Suit No. 2 of 1988. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge and Family Court, upon consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and order dated 30.6.88 decreed the suit and directed the defendant No. 1 to pay Tk. 1,37,000/- against the maintenance and deferred dower and also directed him to pay Tk. 2000/- per month for the maintenance of the plaintiff and her children. The trial court also directed defendant No. 1 to give 5 bighas of land equivalent to the price of 5 bighas of land sold by the plaintiff or in the alternative, he will pay money for 5 (five) bighas of land on the basis of present market value. Defendants, preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1988 (Family) which was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet, who by judgment and decree dated 30.10.93 allowed the appeal in part and set aside the judgment of the trial court directing the defendant No. 1 to pay past maintenance as well as the direction to give 5 (five) bighas of land against dower. The court of appeal below however maintained the decree for maintenance from the date of institution of the suit till the death of the defendant No. 1 on 2.1.91 and also decreed Tk. 10,000/- against deferred dower. It may be mentioned here that during the pendency of the appeal, the defendant No. 1 died on 2.1.91 and the appeal was contested by the defendant No. 2 and her children, the opposite parties No. 2 and 3. 

 5. Mr. M.A. Tariq appearing for the petitioner frankly submits that in view of the conflicting decisions regarding past maintenance, he will not press for past maintenance as given by the Family Court. The learned Advocate, however, submits that the court of appeal below has committed error in setting aside the decree for dower of 5 (five) bighas of land given by Family Court upon misconception of fact and law. In view of the sub-mission of Mr. Tariq, the point involves in this Rule is confined to examine whether the court of appeal below was justified in setting aside the decree of 5 bighas of land given as dower to the plaintiff by the Family Court. 

 6. It appears from the record that notices upon the defendant-opposite parties have duly been served but there is no appearance on behalf of the opposite par-ties. Mr. Md. Tabarak Hossain, learned Advocate appeared in this Rule with the leave of the court and submits that he has instructions on behalf of the opposite par-ties and undertakes to file power on their behalf. In order to facilitate him to file power, 5.2.2002 had been fixed for delivery of judgment though the hearing of the rule was concluded on 30.1.2002. Mr. Hossain failed to file any power on behalf of the opposite parties. Mr. Hossain submitted that the court of appeal below has committed no error of law in setting aside the decree for 5 bighas of land as dower, inasmuch as the dower was already given to the plaintiff by the defendant No. 1. He further submitted that after giving 5 (five) bighas of land by registered deed by the defendant No. 1, as admitted by the plaintiff the Family Court has no power to direct the defendant No. 1 to give further 5 (five) bighas of land on the basis of subsequent agreement. 

 11. It appears from the operating portion of the judgment of the Family Court so far as it relates to passing decree for dower of 5 bighas of land it has passed an imperfect decree which cannot be executed unless the said decree is not modified. The trial court directed the defendant No. 1 to give 5 bighas of land equivalent to the price of 5 (five) bighas of land sold earlier or in the alternative price of 5 bighas of land on the basis of present market value. It will be not possible for the executing court to assess the value of 5 bighas of land. I find above that the defendant No. 1 in fact admitted to give 5 bighas of land indirectly out of schedule 'Kha' land. Accordingly in exercise of suo moto powers. I modify the decree of the Family Court and direct the defendants to execute and register 5 bighas of land out of schedule 'Kha' land within 30 days of the decree. Failing which, the plaintiff shall be at liberty to get 5 (five) bighas of land through the process of the executing proceeding. Accordingly I find substance in this Rule. The Rule succeeds in part. 

 12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute in part without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 30.10.93 of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1988 (Family) reversing those dated 30.6.88 of the learned Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court, Golapganj, Sylhet in Family Suit No. 2 of 1988 so far as in releates to dismissing the suit for dower of 5 (five) bighas of land are set aside. The decree of the court of appeal below directing the defendants to pay maintenance to the plaintiff and her children at the rate of Tk. 2000/- per month from the date of institution of the suit till 2.1.91 and Tk. 10,000/- against deferred dower out of the property left by the defendant No. 1 are hereby maintained. The judgment and decree of the Family Court so far as it relates to 5 (five) bighas of land is maintained subject to the modification that the plaintiff shall get 5 (five) bighas of land out of schedule 'Kha' land and the defendants are hereby directed to give the said land amicably within 30 days of the date of the decree, failing which, the plaintiff is entitled to recover the same through the process of the execution proceedings.
